clue.text: Party game in which Violet Elizabeth's instrument is reportedly sought?

definitions.text: Party game in which Violet Elizabeth's instrument is reportedly sought?

parts.words: Party game in which Violet Elizabeth's instrument is reportedly sought?
parts.note: Violet Elizabeth Bott, the lisping girl in Richmal Crompton's Just William stories, would say cymbal as 'thymbal', so the children's party game where players search for a small sewing cap becomes a hunt for her percussion instrument

explanation.surface: A party game in which children search for a lisping girl's musical instrument.
explanation.walkthrough: Violet Elizabeth in the Just William books lisps, so her 'cymbal' comes out sounding like the sewing item hidden in this traditional children's game.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional children's party game in which one small sewing object is hidden and the players search the room for it.

clue.text: Regularly feed dirt-poor journalist

indicators.note: regularly means taking every second letter of the words that follow, starting from the second

explanation.surface: An instruction to feed someone in desperate poverty at regular intervals.
explanation.definitionFit: An editor is a senior journalist who prepares and oversees what a publication prints.

clue.text: Vintage (ie old) liquid commodity

parts.note: a cru is a vineyard or its wine of a particular quality, so a vintage

indicators.note: liquid suggests something fluid and changeable, so these letters flow into a new order

explanation.surface: A fine old wine described as a tradeable liquid good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'liquid' looks like part of the definition but rearranges IE OLD into DEOIL.
explanation.definitionFit: Unrefined petroleum is one of the world's most heavily traded raw materials on commodity markets.

clue.text: A high-ranking official, old Earl's shuffling round the thone room

indicators.note: round means the shuffled letters go on either side of the other piece
shuffling means the letters of these words are mixed into a new order

parts.note: taken as written for the anagram, the apostrophe ignored
'thone' is the setter's typo for throne; the throne room is jocular for the lavatory, a privy

explanation.surface: An elderly aristocrat shuffles about the royal throne room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'thone' is the setter's misprint for 'throne'; the throne room is a jocular British name for the toilet, and the privy is an old outdoor one.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Privy Seal is one of the great officers of state in the British government, usually a cabinet minister.

clue.text: Notes gold shooting star

parts.note: me and te are two notes of the tonic sol-fa scale
or is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Musical notes made of gold sound like a hit singer.
explanation.definitionFit: A streak of light from space debris burning in the atmosphere is popularly called a shooting star.

clue.text: American support to pass round cocaine that is Mexican property

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes at the end
round means one piece goes around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to pass something to someone is to hand it over
C is a slang abbreviation for cocaine
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: An American helps smuggle drugs, which is how he came to own a Mexican estate.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'support' puts A beneath the rest, so it comes last.
explanation.definitionFit: A hacienda is a large estate or ranch house in Mexico and other Spanish-speaking countries.

clue.text: Where one gets a verruca? Sounds like quite a drag

indicators.note: sounds like says the phrase is to be heard, then written another way

parts.note: a verruca is a wart on the sole, found under the toe of the foot

explanation.surface: Getting a wart on your foot is a real nuisance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drag' looks like slang for a bore, but it is the strong pull of water.
explanation.definitionFit: An undercurrent pulling swimmers away from the shore exerts a strong pull, a drag in the literal sense.

clue.text: Granny's taking little Margaret out to see some of Malaysia

indicators.note: taking means one piece is held by another, so the pieces combine
out says the name goes on the outside of the other piece

parts.note: Peg is a pet form of the name Margaret
nan is a familiar name for a grandmother

explanation.surface: Grandma takes young Margaret on a sightseeing outing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' says the pet name goes on the outside; Peg is a traditional diminutive of Margaret.
explanation.definitionFit: Penang is a state and island off the west coast of peninsular Malaysia, so part of the country.

clue.text: Smartening up, I get stuck into gin/tonic after work

indicators.note: to work something is to manipulate it, so these letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the slash ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone smartens up and gets stuck into a gin and tonic after a day at work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after work' reads as a time; 'after' is fodder and 'work' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gentrification is the upgrading of a run-down district as wealthier residents move in, a smartening up.

clue.text: Director/general manager for Austria in Swiss capital to prop up margin trading

indicators.note: in a down clue the propping piece sits beneath the other, so it comes second
trading suggests exchanging places, so these letters swap into a new order
in means one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: Bern is the capital of Switzerland
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: A manager in Bern props up margin trading on behalf of Austria.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the propping piece sits underneath, so the first name comes first; A is Austria's international car code.
explanation.definitionFit: Ingmar Bergman was the Swedish film director of The Seventh Seal and Wild Strawberries.

clue.text: Bore child — Ethelred's first daughter

parts.note: a tot is a small child

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the following word

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: A child was born to Ethelred, his first daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bore' looks like the past of bear, as in giving birth, but means carried.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear a load is to carry it, so the past tense bore matches carried, a synonym.

clue.text: It's bitter and twisted old Nadine

indicators.note: twisted means the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Old Nadine is a bitter and twisted woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bitter and twisted' is a stock phrase; 'bitter' belongs to the definition and 'twisted' rearranges OLD NADINE.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaves of this common yellow-flowered weed taste bitter and are eaten in salads.

clue.text: Hotel bower to offer shelter

parts.note: Hotel is the radio code word for H
a bower is a leafy shelter, an arbour

explanation.surface: A hotel garden bower offers shelter to guests.
explanation.definitionFit: To harbour someone is to give them refuge, to shelter or protect them.

clue.text: An experienced sailor, Silas is getting to grips with current

indicators.note: getting to grips with means holding, so the name takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: Silas Marner is George Eliot's novel and its title character
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Silas is wrestling with a strong current at sea.
explanation.walkthrough: Silas leads to his surname, MARNER, from George Eliot's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: A mariner is a seaman, especially a seasoned one who navigates a ship.

clue.text: Last in Chemistry, botch A-level for silly hubristic attitude

indicators.note: silly means the letters are messed about into a new order
last in means take the final letter of the word that follows

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written, the hyphen ignored
taken as written

explanation.surface: A student who comes last in Chemistry botches an A-level through silly arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'botch' looks like the anagram signal but is fodder; 'silly' rearranges Y with BOTCH A-LEVEL FOR. An A-level is the English school-leaving exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Being too clever by half means being so pleased with one's own cleverness that it backfires, a kind of arrogance.

clue.text: Is it sung by Rita at Ferdinand?

parts.note: Rita Ora is a British pop singer
at and to are interchangeable in phrases such as at home or to home, loosely
Rio Ferdinand is a former England footballer

explanation.surface: A question whether something was sung by one celebrity to another.
explanation.walkthrough: Rita and Ferdinand are first names standing for the surname and first name of two British celebrities: singer Rita Ora and footballer Rio Ferdinand.
explanation.definitionFit: An oratorio is a large choral work on a religious theme, written to be performed by singers.

clue.text: Annual report of UK takeover of flipping Scottish bank

indicators.note: takeover of means one piece takes the other inside it
report of means the letters are said as a word and written as heard

parts.note: UK, the initials of the United Kingdom, here said aloud as if a single word

indicators.note: flipping means turning the word over so it reads backwards

parts.note: a brae is a Scottish word for a hillside or bank

explanation.surface: A financial report covers a British takeover of a wretched Scottish bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'report of' means UK is pronounced as one syllable rather than as two letters; 'flipping' looks like a mild British curse but turns the hillside word round.
explanation.definitionFit: An annual is a book published once a year, also called a yearbook.

clue.text: Julius christens vessel at sea

parts.note: Julius is the setter, so in his own voice he says I name
SS is the prefix for a steamship

explanation.surface: The setter launches a ship, naming it.
explanation.walkthrough: Setters refer to themselves by their pen name, so 'Julius christens' is 'I name'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at sea in the figurative sense is being confused, all muddled up.

clue.text: Smoothly install archdeacon in Cambridgeshire bishopric

indicators.note: install means put the official title into the other piece

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and diocese in Cambridgeshire
Ven, short for Venerable, is the title of an archdeacon

explanation.surface: A smooth installation of an archdeacon in a Cambridgeshire diocese.
explanation.walkthrough: An archdeacon is styled 'the Venerable', VEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Done evenly means done in a level, regular manner, without bumps, so smoothly.

clue.text: Zinfandel, Asti, Champagne bottles made of flexible material

indicators.note: bottles means the words hold a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Bottles of three wines made of some bendy substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottles' looks like a plural noun but is a verb: the wine names bottle up the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Elastic is stretchy material that springs back to its shape, used in waistbands.

clue.text: Northants opener, subject to medical, to turn up for lunch

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up means the letters read from bottom to top
opener means take the first letter of the word

parts.note: a recruit is accepted if fit, subject to passing a medical

explanation.surface: A Northamptonshire opening batsman needs a fitness test before turning up for lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opener' looks like cricket but takes N; Northants is the English county Northamptonshire, which has a cricket team. Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiffin is an Anglo-Indian word for a light midday meal.

clue.text: Give some stick to Pavlova; by the sound of it, quite some stick!

parts.note: to give someone stick is to jeer them, to boo

indicators.note: by the sound of it says the word is heard, then written as it sounds

parts.note: a pavlova is a meringue dessert

explanation.surface: Someone is told to give a dessert a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' first means criticism, then a thrown stick.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved throwing stick that returns to the thrower is quite a remarkable piece of stick.

clue.text: Match the profile for British police suspect's mugshot

parts.note: an E-fit is a computer-generated likeness of a suspect used by British police

explanation.surface: A British police photofit image matches a suspect's profile.
explanation.walkthrough: An E-FIT is the British police's electronic facial composite of a suspect.
explanation.definitionFit: To befit is to be suitable for, to suit, so to match a profile or role.

clue.text: 2 censoring introduction to scriptures to be fit for consumption

indicators.note: censoring the introduction means the first letter is struck out and replaced

parts.note: the Bible is the Christian scriptures
2 down is EDITOR, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: An editor censors the opening of scripture before it can be published.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' refers to the answer of 2 down, abbreviated to ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible food is safe to eat, so suitable for consumption.

clue.text: Geronimo lapped round astride golden horse

indicators.note: round means the letters are turned to read backwards
astride means the letters straddle the two words

explanation.surface: Geronimo rides round on a golden horse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'astride' picks the letters spanning the two words and 'round' turns them round: geronimO LAPped read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A palomino is a horse with a golden coat and white mane and tail.
